item.title: Kimi Antonelli Takes Pole for United States Grand Prix in Austin
item.description: Photo by: JEROME MIRON Antonelli Delivers When It Matters Most Kimi Antonelli delivered a spectacular qualifying performance on Saturday, securing pole position for the United States Grand Prix at Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas. The Mercedes driver recorded a fastest lap of 1:34.035, beating Max Verstappen by 0.179 seconds to claim the top starting position for Sunday’s race. The result is particularly significant because Antonelli enters the weekend with an opportunity to clinch the 2026 Formula 1 World Championship. The 20 year old Italian has been one of the season’s most consistent drivers, and another victory could bring him closer to securing his first championship. Antonelli’s pole position also marked his seventh of the season and his first since the Belgian Grand Prix in July. After several races without starting at the front, the Mercedes star delivered a crucial performance at the perfect time. Verstappen and Red Bull Remain Dangerous Verstappen will start alongside Antonelli on the front row after qualifying second. The Red Bull driver entered the weekend with considerable momentum after winning the previous two races, but he could not match Antonelli’s pace during the decisive qualifying session. Verstappen’s teammate Isack Hadjar qualified third, giving Red Bull two cars inside the top three. Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc secured fourth, while Lewis Hamilton qualified fifth. Mercedes teammate George Russell struggled during the final qualifying session and finished sixth. His position could become important in the championship battle, as Antonelli currently holds a substantial points advantage. Championship Opportunity Awaits Sunday’s race represents another major opportunity for Antonelli to strengthen his championship position. He has built a 102 point advantage over Russell, with 125 points still available after the Austin race. Antonelli can clinch the championship this weekend if he wins and Russell finishes ninth or lower while Hamilton finishes outside the top four. Otherwise, he will have another opportunity in Mexico. However, the Mercedes driver knows the job is not finished. Verstappen has demonstrated strong race pace recently, and starting from pole does not guarantee victory. Antonelli will need a clean start, consistent pace and a mistake-free performance to convert his qualifying success into another race win. With the championship potentially within reach, all eyes will be on Antonelli when the lights go out in Austin on Sunday.

item.title: Connor Hellebuyck officially reinstated from suspension after trade to Devils
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Stephen R. Sylvanie-Imagn Images Connor Hellebuyck officially reinstated from suspension after trade to Devils appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The long saga between Connor Hellebuyck and the Winnipeg Jets is over. He has officially been traded to the New Jersey Devils and has been reinstated from the suspension that his former team had imposed on him. Connor Hellebucyk has been reinstated from suspension. The #NJDevils now have him at an $8.1M cap hit for this season after his cap hit adjustment for missing training camp. They have $103K projected cap space. https://t.co/zVQ4w9zWSd Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — PuckPedia (@PuckPedia) October 24, 2026 Hellebuyck had let the Jets know during the offseason that he wanted to be traded by the team and was willing to waive his no-trade contract. However, when the team still hadn’t moved him before the start of Winnipeg’s training camp in September, he refused to report. As a result, the dispute between the goaltender and the Jets went public. Hellebuyck was suspended when he didn’t show up at training camp. Since he has not been with any team until this point, he will need to get into game shape before the Devils can activate him and put him in the lineup. His goal is to get into game shape quickly and help the Devils win a Stanley Cup. Goaltending has not been a strength for the Devils to this point. Jake Allen and Nico Daws, who was involved in the trade to Winnipeg, had been stopping 88 percent of the shots they had face in the early part of the season. That ranked 23rd among goaltending tandems. Hellebuyck is one of the most accomplished regular-season goaltenders in the NHL. He has won three Vezina Trophies and a Hart Trophy as the league MVP. He also led the United States to a gold medal at the 2026 Winter Olympics, but his playoff record has not been as good. item.title: Why even Kevin Durant would love to take this skill from Mavericks’ Kyrie Irving
item.description: Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images Why even Kevin Durant would love to take this skill from Mavericks’ Kyrie Irving appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Dusty May scored his first ever win with the Dallas Mavericks and as an NBA coach against the Indiana Pacers as Kyrie Irving poured in 24 points before revealing an ongoing injury situation. Star forward Cooper Flagg was hit on the fast break by Aaron Nesmith and suffered a shoulder injury that got a major update . Another star forward, Kevin Durant of the Houston Rockets, has been watching the Mavericks this season, keying in on Irving based on comments made to the NBA’s official X account recently. NBA players were asked which skill they would steal from another player if they could, calling to mind the classic movie ‘Space Jam,’ and Durant gave an interesting answer. “None, I feel like I have them all,” Durant said. “I would say Kyrie’s ball handling,” Durant added without hesitation. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Irving led the Cleveland Cavaliers to an NBA championship in 2016, helping to defeat Stephen Curry’s Golden State Warriors with a masterful display of smooth moves, layups and jump shots. His age (34) has come into focus on a young Flagg-led Mavericks team this season, but so far, Irving has been a leader both on and off the court. May was given a mop bucket bath as he headed into the locker room after the Mavericks’ first win, showing his players are perhaps even more excited than him about what the 2026-27 NBA season could hold. The Mavericks’ season has plenty of promise and Irving is a big reason why. His game, and his skills, are timeless, and he is surrounded by talented players who appear to fit his skillset to a tee. item.title: Antonelli Surprises Mercedes With US GP Pole as Title Chance Grows
item.description: Andrea Kimi Antonelli has one hand on the F1 title after securing US GP pole position, with both of the other contenders below him. Mercedes ’ Antonelli came into F1 qualifying without the pace that the Ferrari pair of Lewis Hamilton & Charles Leclerc had, along with Red Bull’s Max Verstappen. The Italian showed enough, but was not as strong as the other three drivers. However, as it has been this year, Antonelli put in a superlative performance, even exceeding expectations of Mercedes to claim F1 pole in the US GP – putting himself in the prime position to potentially secure his first drivers’ championship. Antonelli Relays How F1 US GP Qualifying Panned Out “It’s been a good qualifying session where we progressed throughout the session,” Antonelli said in the press conference after the F1 US GP qualifying. “But yeah, it was not an easy session. The wind was picking up. “It was quite gusty, and Q3 was a little bit tricky because the wind was a bit unpredictable. It picked up as well, especially that last lap and it felt a bit worse, but overall, yeah, I’m happy because we’ve been working really hard on this package, and we’re still trying to understand it fully. “But since Singapore, we’ve taken a big step further, and now we just have to keep working on it, keep understanding it. But yeah, it’s a good result for the team because they’ve done a tremendous job bringing this package, and finally, we’re seeing the results,” summed up Antonelli, who, like Toto Wolff, was surprised to be on pole. Antonelli Relieved Track Limits Didn’t Hurt Amid Surprise Pole The biggest achievement was no track limits after struggling with it all season long, even at the Circuit of the Americas. “It was surprising, but also one of the biggest achievements for me today is that I didn’t do track limits,” chuckled Antonelli. “So that also made our life a little bit easier, that I didn’t put myself in a difficult situation. “We were just able to progress throughout the session and to build from there. But definitely, it was unexpected. We knew we’d be close, but yeah, it was a good surprise,” summed up Antonelli, who is on the brink of making history if things align on Sunday, if he wins the US GP, and his rivals are not close to him. If Antonelli wins and Hamilton finishes fifth or lower, while George Russell finishes ninth or lower, the Italian will be crowned the youngest-ever F1 drivers’ champion. item.title: Houston's Joshua Van to defend his flyweight title against Manel Kape at UFC 336 in January
item.description: Houston's Joshua Van reacts with Joe Rogan after a victory against Alexandre Pantoja of Brazil in the UFC flyweight championship fight during the UFC 331 event at Crypto.com Arena on September 19, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Chris Unger/Zuffa LLC) Joshua Van cemented himself as the class of UFC's flyweight division with his dominant win over Alexandre Pantoja in September . Now, he'll get another chance to prove it when he faces Manel Kape, the only flyweight ranked in the top four that the Houston fighter hasn't already defeated. Van (18-2) will defend his flyweight title against Kape (23-7) at UFC 336 on Jan. 30 at Toronto's Scotiabank Arena. The 25-year-old Van, who was born in Myanmar but has lived in Houston since he was 12 years old, has taken the flyweight division by storm over the past 16 months and can thank Kape for giving him an opportunity. Van stepped in to fight Brandon Royval on short notice in June 2025 when Kape pulled out of the bout with a broken foot. Van won a thrilling decision that night and was awarded with a Fight of the Night bonus. His career took off from there, taking the title from Alexandre Pantoja in his next fight, then successfully defending it twice in a row, including September's victory over Pantoja in a rematch. The 32-year-old Kape, who is from Angola, also has been on the rise since getting healthy, including a knockout of Royval and a stoppage of Kyoji Horiguchi in June. The No. 1 contender in the division also been calling out Van along the way. "You're all going to be surprised by how easy I make this fight look," Kape posted on Twitter shortly after Van beat Pantoja for a second time. Van responded that Kape, who blew a weight cut in 2024 and is one of the biggest flyweights in the UFC, needs to focus on making weight. "Start cutting now cuz u better make weight!!" Van wrote on Twitter last month . "We don't want another weight excuse. Let's give the people what they want!!!" Also at UFC 336, undefeated Michael Morales will battle Carlos Prates for the interim welterweight title with the winner earning the right to face Islam Makhachev, who has dominated the weight class for the past year but was forced to withdraw from a showdown with Prates. item.title: Max Verstappen refuses to celebrate US GP qualifying result: 'No need to smile'
item.description: Motorsport photo After qualifying second for the United States Grand Prix, Max Verstappen has said there is "no need to smile and be super happy" about his performance. A lack of grip in Q3 left him unable to fight for pole, which instead went to Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli. The Red Bull driver ended up 0.179 seconds behind the young Italian at the Circuit of the Americas, and only 0.036s ahead of team-mate Isack Hadjar in third - his best qualifying result yet. But while the Dutchman was looking to be a pole contender earlier in the session, an unexpected lack of grip left him wanting more. “Q1 and Q2 I felt really good. I mean, I did my first lap in Q2 just on a used set," he said. "So when I went to Q3, I had high hopes, but unfortunately, it just felt bad. Like I just didn’t really have the grip that I wanted, so I couldn’t lean on the rear that I wanted in the final sector and that just cost me too much time. "And then I mean, when you look at the sheets and you are starting P2 it's nice and it’s a good result, but I was hoping for more and this was just not it. But if it’s, let’s say, not a great feeling in qualifying and then that’s a P2, I’ll take it. But there’s no need to then smile and be super happy about it.” Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing He ran only six laps in Q2 to save tyres, but rejected the suggestion that the switch from used to fresh rubber was to blame. “No problem normally. I’ve done that many times before. I’ve even qualified once with only two sets," he revealed. "So yeah, there is no explanation why in Q3 it just didn’t come together, or apart from the last lap where I think everyone struggled for lap time. But it’s something that we have to look at because it’s very odd of course that you have, let’s say, the best feeling on a used set.” It is still a strong result for Red Bull, with Hadjar, who also felt good on used tyres in Q2, directly behind him in third. Verstappen has been the circuit’s loudest critic this weekend, after describing the bumps at COTA as “unacceptable” and “out of control” on Thursday. From the front row, he will have the chance to attack Antonelli up the hill into Turn 1, where the worst of those bumps sit. Verstappen, fourth in the standings on 221 points, is chasing a third straight victory after success in Malaysia and Singapore. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Virgil van Dijk on Momentum and Making Winning a Habit
item.description: Liverpool’s past three games haven’t seen the Reds looking perfect but they have all ended in victory—and brought plenty of goals along the way, both for and against. In those three wins against LASK, Brentford, and Villarreal they’ve scored 12 times and conceded seven. Certainly, then, it’s been exciting. And, in the end, they’ve deserved all three wins on balance. All of which means they appear to have a little momentum to carry with them into Sunday’s league tie against Brighton. “Momentum is a big thing in football, and it is important that we maintain ours,” club captain Virgil van Dijk noted ahead of the match. “After three wins in a row there is definitely a good feeling within the group, but that will count for nothing unless we follow up with another strong performance. “Brighton arrive in great form and will provide a really good test for us—we will need to be at our very best if we want to come away with all three points. I think Tuesday night’s win over Villarreal showed we are moving in the right direction, but we still have a long way to go.” Van Dijk himself was shaky to start the mid-week European tie against Villarreal, with the Reds going down 2-0 before waking up and dominating most of the rest of the way to take the game 4-3 and keep their league phase Champions League record perfect. In the end, though, it’s the win that matters. It’s the battling back that matters. It’s scoring more goals than the opposition that matters—whether that means getting a 1-0 or 4-3 victory at the end of the day. “The first half hour in particular was not the best,” Van Dijk added. “I definitely include myself in that, and we found ourselves behind—deservedly so. But if that was the negative side, the positive was the way we responded. We battled our way back into the game and our performance in the second half was much improved “I said before Villarreal that winning is a habit, and it is a habit that breeds confidence within a squad. I think you could see that on Tuesday. We knew the opening wasn’t good enough, but we reacted in exactly the right way and the attitude we showed, the work we put in, was rewarded.”

item.title: Instant reactions to Alabama's comeback win vs. Texas A&M
item.description: Coming off back-to-back losses the last two weeks, the Alabama Crimson Tide badly needed to get back in the win column Saturday afternoon at home against a struggling Texas A&M team. The Aggies came to Tuscaloosa sitting at 4-3 overall (1-3 SEC) for the season, and had yet to score in double digits in either of their two SEC road games previously. Texas A&M snapped that skid Saturday afternoon though in the first half alone, entering the locker room tied with Alabama at 17-17 after the Crimson Tide struggled in a number of areas prior to halftime, even despite starting the game with two picks defensively. Some of those same struggles carried over into the second half, but Alabama went on to turn the tide starting late in the third quarter. Alabama then owned the fourth quarter on both sides of the ball with a 14-0 edge in the game's final 15 minutes, eventually picking up a 31-20 win . Here are some instant reactions to Alabama's win against Texas A&M on Saturday afternoon. Rico Scott, Fatutoa Henry step up for Tide Still without Ryan Coleman-Williams due to injury, Alabama needed someone to step up Saturday against the Aggies at wide receiver, and Rico Scott delivered in a big way, as did Fatutoa Henry along the Tide's defensive front. Scott had a monster game by hauling in six receptions for 156 yards, while Henry also had a huge performance, finishing with four tackles and two sacks. Alabama's third down offensive struggles continue After a rough showing a week ago against Tennessee on third down, Alabama's offense saw some of those similar struggles Saturday against the Aggies. Alabama, whose second third down conversion did not come until the final play of the third quarter, finished the game going 5-of-12 on third downs. Alabama's defense has solid performance While it was not pretty at times, it was overall a solid showing from the Crimson Tide defense. Alabama limited the Aggies to only 278 yards of total offense, while also limiting to Texas A&M to a combined 4-of-12 on third-and-fourth down. The Tide also forced three Aggie turnovers. Alabama's bye week arrives Following the win against Texas A&M, Alabama's bye week now arrives at the perfect time with the Tide dealing with a number of injuries on both sides of the ball. Alabama's next game will come in Week 10 on the road at LSU. item.title: NC State fires Dave Doeren, replaces him with Todd Goebel
item.description: Sergio Estrada-Imagn Images NC State fires Dave Doeren, replaces him with Todd Goebel appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . NC State football took a rough 31-28 loss to struggling Stanford Friday. Which added to an already strange 2026 that featured the Wolfpack’s infamous finish against Vanderbilt . But the Stanford loss now costed head coach Dave Doeren his job. Doeren got fired Saturday nearly 24 hours after the stunning defeat to the Cardinal. College Football insider Nicole Auerbach helped report the move, along with who replaces Doeren. “Todd Goebbel, NC State running backs coach/special teams coordinator, will serve as interim head coach for the remainder of the season,” Auerbach posted on the social media website X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Doeren created a new competitive brand in Raleigh after he took the gig in 2013. His first Wolfpack team went 3-9, but later played in 10 bowl games from there. Doeren still posted a 4-6 record in postseason contests, though. He’ll leave with a 98-74 overall mark there, making him the program’s winningest head coach ever. And this is a Wolfpack program that was once led by coaching legends Chuck Amato and the late Lou Holtz. But despite the wins, Doeren struggled to dominate in the College Football Transfer Portal . Plus had difficulty surpassing the nine-win mark each season. ESPN college football insider Pete Thamel revealed what the school will now owe Doeren. “NC State will owe Doeren nearly $10.3 million, which is subject to offset and mitigation, per his contract. He had three years remaining on his deal,” Thamel said via the social media website X, formerly Twitter. So now NC State rises as the second Power Four opening during the week of Oct. 19, joining Maryland after firing Mike Locksley . With the victory, the Crimson Tide remained in the hunt for a College Football Playoff berth as it enters its lone idle date of the season. Here are a few instant thoughts on the Crimson Tide's performance: Talking points on Alabama football 1) Alabama WR Rico Scott had a career day against the Aggies, crossing the 100-yard receiving mark by halftime and accounting for much of UA's total offense. UA wide receivers have largely struggled to get open since Ryan Coleman-Williams was injured, especially in a Week 7 loss to Tennessee. Scott had the look of a go-to option for QB Keelon Russell on Saturday, however, and it came not a moment too soon for offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb. He finished with 156 yards, a career-best. 2) A lack of discipline on Alabama's part had a hand in multiple A&M scoring drives, including a 15-yard defensive pass interference call on Dijon Lee (more on him in a minute), and a roughing the passer (with a targeting ejection) that ended Red Morgan's day in the second quarter. Then there was an offsides flag on DB Chuck McDonald that gave Texas A&M a first down to open the second half, a series that ended with an Aggies field goal. The Crimson Tide entered play ranked a woeful 90th in the country in penalties with 7.1 per game. item.title: Postgame Thoughts: Tease in Tuscaloosa
item.description: TUSCALOOSA, ALABAMA - OCTOBER 24: Mario Craver #1 of the Texas A&M Aggies is tackled from behind by Luke Metz #4 of the Alabama Crimson Tide during the first quarter at Bryant-Denny Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Tuscaloosa, Alabama. (Photo by Jason Clark/Getty Images) | Getty Images Texas A&M showed us in this game what has made them a 4-4 team. Then they showed us why they were a preseason top 10 team. And then they showed us that first part again. A different path, but a familiar result, as the Aggies fall 31-20 to No. 13 Alabama in Tuscaloosa. The game started off about as badly as you could have imagined, with Marcel Reed throwing a pick six just a few plays into the team’s first offensive possession, then throwing an even more egregious interception on the first play of the next drive. It looked for a moment that we would see backup QB Brady Hart enter the game, as he began throwing on the sidelines, but that never came to fruition, and for a while, that seemed fortuitous. After an Alabama missed FG, Marcel Reed led the Ags down the field with surprising poise or a touchdown drive to tie the game. From there it was very much a back and forth affair, but through most of it, Reed appeared to be in control of the offense and delivering on-target throws more consistently than he has in perhaps any other game this season. The defense was making things hard on Alabama QB Keelon Russell on third downs. It was tied at halftime. A&M had the lead through three quarters. This was a game that was very much there for the taking. Then Bama took it. Somehow, the fourth quarter suddenly looked like the A&M team we have seen for the most of SEC play, a vulnerable defense and an overmatched offense folded when it mattered most. Bama scored a TD on consecutive drives, and the A&M offense didn’t get a single first down in the final frame, sealing the deal on yet another SEC loss as the Aggies drop to 1-4 in conference play. Certainly the Aggies looked improved in this game compared to lopsided road losses to LSU and Missouri. There was a long stretch of this game where they not only showed life, but actually looked capable of pulling off the upset. But unfortunately, there was just as much of the fatal flaws this team has exhibited all season long. No moral victories here. The Aggies now enter the bye week hoping to find something that can get this team to bowl eligibility and salvage something out of what continues to be one of the more disappointing seasons in recent memory.

item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
